text.content:
The thin-blooded are the fourteenth and fifteenth generations of Caine's line, the weakest and most recently Embraced Kindred in existence — sometimes called the Last Generations because certain passages of the Book of Nod are read as naming the clanless and thin-blooded as harbingers of Gehenna. The thin-blooded themselves are almost universally unaware of any such destiny; they know only that their weak blood, high generation and obscure origins earn them contempt from the rest of Kindred society. Both the Camarilla and the Sabbat generally treat them as unwanted baggage, tools or dangerous weapons to be controlled or destroyed. The Anarch Movement is the only faction that offers them anything resembling a fair shake, though even there acceptance is not universal: some anarchs are outright abusive or exploitative, most are marginally welcoming and treat thin-bloods as useful allies of convenience, and thin-bloods are typically kept on probationary status until they prove themselves.

What Defines a Thin-Blood

Fourteenth and fifteenth generation vampires are collectively the Last Generations. Roughly half of all fourteenth-generation Kindred are Caitiff, with the remainder belonging to their sire's clan; all fifteenth-generation vampires are Caitiff without exception, since at that dilution the Curse of Caine can no longer sustain a clan's defining characteristics. Virtually all thin-blooded vampires follow the Path of Humanity — they simply haven't had time to encounter, or need for, an alternate morality.

Character Creation for the Last Generations

Creating a thin-blooded character follows the normal five-step vampire chargen process, with these exceptions:

  • Attributes: Fourteenth- and fifteenth-generation characters assign only six Traits (rather than seven) in their primary Attribute category, still five in their secondary and three in their tertiary, exactly like other vampires otherwise.
  • Generation: The player decides whether the character is fourteenth or fifteenth generation. Either choice requires taking the matching Generation Flaw (Fourteenth Generation or Fifteenth Generation); no Background Traits are spent on Generation, and taking either Flaw prohibits also taking the Generation Background. Trait maximums otherwise match those of thirteenth-generation vampires.
  • Disciplines: Thin-blooded vampires begin play with only two Basic Discipline powers and can never raise a Discipline above Intermediate. Fourteenth-generation vampires may eventually learn both Intermediate powers of a Discipline; fifteenth-generation vampires may only ever learn the first Intermediate power of a given Discipline. A fourteenth-generation vampire who belongs to a clan may only choose starting Discipline powers available to that clan; a clanless (Caitiff) thin-blood may choose any starting Discipline powers she can justify having learned.
  • Backgrounds: The Last Generations may take the same Background Traits as any other vampire, within reason — Influence and celebrity-adjacent Backgrounds are unusual but not forbidden. They may also uniquely take the new Insight Background (see the Backgrounds compendium).
  • Merits and Flaws: Thin-bloods can take any Merit or Flaw open to other vampires, though some don't fit well (a fourteenth-generation Caitiff is unlikely to have a Prestigious Sire or be owed a Debt of Gratitude). "Mortal" Merits like Blush of Health, Eat Food (free for fifteenth-generation characters), Light Sleeper and Calm Heart are common and thematically appropriate given the Last Generations' relative proximity to humanity. Three Flaws specifically define the thin-blooded: Fourteenth Generation, Fifteenth Generation and Thin Blood. A character taking Fourteenth Generation may also take Thin Blood if desired (many, but not all, fourteenth-generation vampires are thin-blooded); a character taking Fifteenth Generation may not also take Thin Blood, since the Fifteenth Generation Flaw already folds in (with slightly different wording) everything Thin Blood covers.

Core Thin-Blood Weaknesses

The Fourteenth Generation, Fifteenth Generation and Thin Blood Flaws (see the Merits & Flaws compendium for full text) share a common shape: doubled Blood Trait costs for healing, raising Physical Attributes and fueling Disciplines; an inability to reliably create blood bonds or ghouls; and an Embrace that can fail outright (a Simple Test determines whether a would-be childe survives Embrace or ends up an inconvenient mortal corpse). Fifteenth-generation vampires take lethal rather than aggravated damage from sunlight, cannot sire progeny by the Embrace at all, and can eat and hold down mortal food for about an hour. Vampires below fourteenth generation may still take the Thin Blood Flaw on its own, but cannot invent new Disciplines the way the Last Generations sometimes can, and cannot take the Insight Background.

Additional Thin-Blooded Rules

Anomalous Biological Activity and Aging: Whenever a thin-blooded vampire heals a level of aggravated damage, she may spontaneously experience minor reactivated mortal functions — growing stubble, feeling hungry for real food, producing real saliva, and similar effects — at the Storyteller's discretion. This can help a thin-blood pass a witch-hunter's scrutiny, but many elders find it disturbing and react badly to witnessing it. Thin-blooded vampires do not actually age from this effect alone; only the Ravaging Years Flaw causes true aging.

Waking Up: Despite rumor, thin blood grants no inherent advantage or disadvantage when it comes to waking or acting during daylight hours.

Roleplaying a Thin-Blood

A thin-blooded character is a walking contradiction: a comparative weakling among vampiric giants and a novice among vipers, whose survival is chancy at best, but whose innocence of Kindred society offers a fresh, unique perspective on the night. Most thin-bloods are not drawn from the exceptional or unusual, unlike most vampires — they tend to be average mortals in life: lovers Embraced in passion, a vessel spared out of guilt, a friend or relative Embraced on a whim, or even an enemy given undeath as a curse. Many never learn who Embraced them or why.
